title: Conditional machine space bound
statement: Let $D,M_1,M_2$ be finite Turing machines over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ be a Boolean word, let $b$ be a Boolean, and let $T,t$ be natural numbers. Suppose $D$ computes the one-symbol output $[b]$ on input $x$ in exactly $T$ steps. The space used by the conditional machine on input $x$ through step $t$ is at most the sum of the space used by $D$ through step $T$, the space used by the branch machine selected by $b$ through step $t$, and $2$.
hypotheses_covered: $D$ computes output $[b]$ on $x$ in exactly $T$ steps
